title: Myth Flip — "heart trouble is a men's problem" (Reena, 46)
caption:
Myth: heart disease is a men's problem. It kills about 1 in 3 women, and fewer than half of us know that (American Heart Association). Ask for three numbers: BP, LDL, A1c.
Which myth should we flip next? 👇
www.aiforheratx.org
#womenshealth #hearthealth #knowyournumbers #womenover40 #healthmyths

scenes.text: Reena is 46 and she's been tired since March in a way that sleep doesn't touch.
phrases: Reena's 46. Two teenagers, a job, cold chai on the counter.
Tired since March in a way sleep doesn't fix.
Her doctor checked her thyroid and said it was stress.
Nobody mentioned her blood pressure or her cholesterol.

scenes.text: Women's heart attacks often arrive as exhaustion, jaw ache or nausea, not the movie chest-clutch (AHA).
phrases: Her mum's heart attack had looked like one bad week.
No clutched chest, no dramatic collapse, nothing like the films.
The AHA says women more often get jaw pain, nausea, breathlessness.
So the myth wasn't harmless. It cost her mum hours.

scenes.text: Put BP, LDL and A1c in your notes app tonight, then ask for all three at your next visit.
phrases: Three things in your notes app: BP, LDL, A1c.
Ask for all three at your next visit (AHA, Life's Essential 8, 2022).
Walk 20 minutes on five days. That's the WHO's 150 a week.
And one sentence out loud: "Please put that in my chart."
